Subject: ApexMind — quick fleet check + possible standby hold

Team —

ApexMind (James) is asking for a short window to secure dedicated capacity for a Q2 production ramp. They expect to ramp to ~80 concurrent inference slots (short sequences, ~512 tokens) and estimate 4M tokens/day at peak. Sales asked for a 30–45 day standby hold while they finish procurement and provide a PO.

Can Diego/Marcus confirm:
- Current available GPU inventory across us-west/us-east that could support 80 concurrent slots for a 30-day standby (assume baseline model is davinci-xxl-like; we may use quantized variant).
- Any constraints by instance type/region (we prefer to keep primary in us-west).
- Recommended hold mechanism: a soft reservation in our Dedicated pool vs. formal capacity hold (pros/cons).

I've attached the capacity request XLSX from ApexMind (apexmind_capacity_request.xlsx) and their rough ramp doc. James — copying you so we're aligned on ask.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, James Park <james@apexmind.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ApexMind — quick fleet check + possible standby hold

Karthik —

Quick inventory snapshot (as of 01-Feb-2028):
- us-west: 120 usable A100-class GPUs; 40 already reserved to other Dedicated customers with firm contracts; ~80 flexible for staging/soft-holds if we re-balance some spare capacity.
- us-east: 70 usable A100-class GPUs; 20 reserved; ~50 flexible.
- On-prem/private pools: not applicable for this customer unless they sign Private.

Notes / considerations:
- For 80 concurrent slots at ~512 tokens and model throughput similar to a 70B dense model, we'd recommend either: (a) quantized 8-bit variant on A100x2 nodes with batching to shave unit cost, or (b) reserve 40 A100 nodes in us-west with autoscale headroom.
- Soft reservation: we can implement a time-boxed standby (30–45 days) by tagging a capacity bucket and preventing new ephemeral allocations into it; this is low-friction but not SLA-backed.
- Formal hold (contract level): requires a reserved capacity commit (Dedicated) and coordination with finance & legal for billing/credits. This gives better guarantees but is slower.

I'll attach a quick sizing matrix. Marcus — can you sketch a recommended allocation plan (soft vs formal) and the rollback/fallback policy?

Diego
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: sizing_matrix_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, James Park <james@apexmind.ai>, Procurement <procure@apexmind.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Feb 2028 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ApexMind — quick fleet check + possible standby hold

Diego / Karthik —

Proposed plan based on Diego's inventory and ApexMind's profile: 
1) Phase 0 (soft standby, 30 days): Tag 40 A100 GPUs in us-west as "APX-standby". This prevents ephemeral placements but allows rapid reassign with 24–48h notice if higher-priority committed customers need them.
2) Phase 1 (formal commit if PO arrives within 30 days): Convert the tag to a Dedicated temporary allocation of 40 nodes with a 3-month minimum billing window. Apply 10% ramping credit if they commit to the 3-month term.
3) Fallback: If we need to free capacity, we shift traffic to us-east (latency + cost delta documented) and fall back to a quantized model variant with 15% throughput reduction but 35% cost savings.

Operational asks: 
- Legal/Finance needs a short standby terms doc for procurement to accept (one-pager). I drafted a starter (standby_terms_draft.docx).
- We need a 24h automated notice window for any preemption during the soft standby. Can we surface that in console?

If Grace signs off, I'll mark the 40 GPUs and notify support & SRE.

Marcus
Product Ops — Capacity Planning
